paragraphs: Choosing a learning rate is a consequential part of foundation model pretraining. Methods that transfer settings from smaller experiments can help, but the paper describes restrictions on when those transfers work and the cost of tuning proxy models. AdaLRS instead searches for a suitable learning rate while training is already underway.

Its search signal is the speed at which training loss decreases. The authors provide theoretical and experimental analyses connecting the best learning rate for pretraining loss with the best rate for its descent velocity, reporting convexity and a shared optimum in their analysis. This relationship motivates using observed loss dynamics to guide adjustments with few additional computations. They also provide a theoretical convergence guarantee.

Experiments on language and vision-language model pretraining show AdaLRS moving initially suboptimal rates into the neighborhood of the optimum and improving model performance. Tests span model sizes, training paradigms, underlying learning-rate schedules, and hyperparameter settings. The contribution is an online adjustment mechanism whose reported effectiveness extends across these tested configurations.
neurips-2025-adalrs-loss-guided-adaptive.tldr: AdaLRS uses training-loss dynamics to adjust learning rates online, improving pretraining efficiency and performance across tested settings.

paragraphs: A video representation can capture what appears in a scene while poorly distinguishing how it changes. This paper makes that distinction explicit through chiral action recognition: separating temporally opposite actions such as opening and closing a door. These pairs demand sensitivity to changes in state, position, size, or count, and many existing video embeddings represent them poorly.

The authors develop a self-supervised adaptation method that operates on sequences of frozen image features. An autoencoder gives its latent space a structural bias inspired by perceptual straightening. The objective is a compact representation in which opposite actions can be separated by a linear classifier, making temporal direction accessible through a simple decision boundary.

Evaluations on Something-Something, EPIC-Kitchens, and Charade show that the resulting representation outperforms much larger pretrained video models on the proposed task. Combining it with existing models also improves classification on standard benchmarks. Together, these findings suggest that the learned temporal information complements capabilities already present in those models.
neurips-2025-chirality-in-action-time-aw.tldr: A self-supervised adaptation method produces compact video representations that distinguish temporally opposite actions and complement existing video models.

paragraphs: In online learning, regret compares the learner’s accumulated loss with what an alternative decision rule would have achieved. Phi-regret allows that alternative to transform the learner’s actions. This paper studies guarantees that adapt to the particular transformation used for comparison, building on earlier bounds tied to a sparsity-based measure of transformation complexity.

The central contribution is a prior distribution over binary transformations. The authors show that obtaining regret guarantees dependent on this prior is sufficient to obtain their improved comparator-adaptive bound. They then give two efficient constructions: one combines copies of kernelized Hedge, while the other combines copies of a variant of the Blum–Mansour reduction. Both simplify the algorithmic route to the guarantee.

The second construction also extends to a class of general-sum games, where it yields accelerated, adaptive convergence to Phi-equilibria. For correlated equilibria, a special case, the reported bound improves on existing results. The contribution therefore links stronger individual learning guarantees with improved convergence guarantees in the stated game setting.
neurips-2025-comparator-adaptive-phi-reg.tldr: A prior over action transformations yields simpler algorithms with improved adaptive regret bounds and stronger equilibrium-convergence guarantees for a class of games.

paragraphs: Previously collected experience can reduce the amount of new interaction needed for reinforcement learning, but source and target environments may respond differently to the same actions. Methods that filter or penalize mismatched transitions depend on measuring this difference. The paper highlights that some existing measures can be ill-defined when the environments’ transition distributions have disjoint support.

CompFlow models target dynamics using a conditional flow that starts from the output distribution of a source-domain flow. This makes the source model part of the target model’s construction, rather than learning target dynamics directly from Gaussian noise. A connection between flow matching and optimal transport supports both improved target-dynamics generalization and a Wasserstein-distance estimate of the dynamics gap.

The method then actively gathers data in regions with large estimated differences. The authors theoretically show that this exploration strategy reduces the performance gap relative to an optimal policy. Experiments across several benchmarks with shifted dynamics report improvements over strong baselines, supporting the combined modeling and data-collection approach.
neurips-2025-composite-flow-matching-for.tldr: CompFlow builds target dynamics on a source flow model and uses estimated dynamics differences to guide exploration under environment shifts.

paragraphs: Multilingual language models need text that is both linguistically diverse and sufficiently clean for learning. DCAD-2000 addresses these needs through a corpus assembled from newly extracted Common Crawl material and existing multilingual sources. It contains 46.72 TB of text across 8.63 billion documents and covers 2,282 languages and 159 writing scripts, including 155 high- and medium-resource languages.

The methodological contribution concerns how this material is cleaned. Instead of relying on manually chosen heuristic thresholds, the authors frame cleaning as anomaly detection. The resulting dynamic filter automatically identifies and removes content judged noisy or anomalous. This changes the cleaning problem from choosing fixed rules by hand to detecting unusual content within a filtering framework.

The authors report improved data quality and cleaning-pipeline robustness, alongside downstream gains from fine-tuning language models on the corpus. Improvements are particularly notable for low-resource languages across multiple multilingual benchmarks. The contribution therefore combines broader language coverage with a cleaning approach supported by reported benefits in subsequent model performance.
neurips-2025-dcad-2000-a-multilingual-da.tldr: DCAD-2000 combines text from 2,282 languages with anomaly-based cleaning and reports downstream gains, especially for low-resource languages.

paragraphs: Video temporal grounding locates the portions of a long video that match a language query. The paper examines a weakness in how existing systems connect language to video: treating text tokens uniformly can conceal their different roles. Controlled experiments show excessive reliance on the end-of-sequence token’s overall sentence meaning, with word-level information used less effectively.

DualGround explicitly separates these sources of meaning into two branches. One routes the end-of-sequence token through a sentence-level path. The other groups word tokens into phrases for more localized matching. Role-aware interactions connect video features with these distinct semantic levels, while a joint framework brings their contributions together.

This structure allows a query’s overall meaning and its more specific phrases to influence temporal alignment in different ways. The authors report state-of-the-art results for moment retrieval and highlight detection across QVHighlights and Charades-STA. These findings support their claim that explicitly organizing sentence and phrase information improves both broad alignment and fine-grained video grounding.
neurips-2025-empower-words-dualground-fo.tldr: DualGround separates sentence-level and phrase-level language signals to improve localization of relevant moments and highlights in videos.

paragraphs: Noisy pretraining labels can have an unintuitive effect: accuracy within the training distribution may improve while generalization elsewhere deteriorates. This paper systematically investigates that effect, called catastrophic inheritance, in medical models. The setting matters because medical annotations are scarce, pretraining sources can be noisy, and shifts between domains can be substantial.

Controlled label-corruption experiments connect increasing noise with declining skewness and kurtosis in feature and output-score distributions. These statistics describe aspects of distribution shape. The authors interpret their decline as evidence of flattened representations with less discriminative detail, particularly relevant to fine-grained tasks such as histopathology. They use the statistics as compact, interpretable markers of degradation.

The proposed response adds two scalar regularizers to the fine-tuning loss to restore skewness and kurtosis. It keeps the backbone unchanged and adds negligible overhead. Tests on PLIP models trained with Twitter pathology images and other large vision and language backbones report consistent robustness and cross-domain accuracy gains across varied noise levels.
neurips-2025-from-pretraining-to-patholo.tldr: The paper links inherited pretraining noise to changes in representation statistics and improves medical-model robustness with two lightweight regularizers.

paragraphs: This paper studies reinforcement learning problems that continue indefinitely and optimize average reward while respecting constraints. Its policy class is generally parameterized, with the stated requirement that policy gradients be smooth and bounded. The goal is to establish how quickly learning approaches a globally optimal solution while also reducing constraint violations.

The authors propose a primal-dual natural actor-critic algorithm and analyze both forms of progress together. When the learner knows the environment’s mixing time, they obtain global-convergence and constraint-violation rates of O-tilde(1/sqrt(T)) over a learning horizon of length T. The tilde notation suppresses logarithmic factors. Thus, the guarantee addresses reward optimization and constraint satisfaction at the same reported order.

Without knowledge of mixing time, the rates become O-tilde(1/T^(0.5−epsilon)), provided T is at least O-tilde(tau_mix^(2/epsilon)). This is a conditional guarantee with an explicit horizon requirement. The authors report matching the theoretical lower bound for Markov decision processes, positioning the analysis as a stronger theoretical foundation for average-reward constrained learning.
neurips-2025-global-convergence-for-aver.tldr: A primal-dual natural actor-critic algorithm achieves global convergence and constraint guarantees whose rates depend on whether mixing time is known.

paragraphs: Inferring an image’s geographic location requires combining visual clues at different levels with knowledge about the world. A broad scene impression and a small local detail can contribute differently to that decision. GRE Suite addresses the paper’s diagnosis that existing geolocation approaches lack sufficiently structured reasoning and explainability.

The suite includes a dataset, a model, and an evaluation benchmark. GRE30K provides geographic reasoning data intended to support fine-grained visual and contextual analysis. The GRE model uses multiple reasoning stages to infer scene attributes, local details, and semantic features, progressively narrowing the possible regions. This organizes location inference into intermediate reasoning steps.

GREval-Bench evaluates urban, natural, and landmark scenes at both broad and fine scales, including continent or country and city or street. The authors report significant improvements over existing methods across all evaluated localization granularities. The findings support structured reasoning as an effective component of the tested geolocation system, while the suite provides resources for both training and measuring that capability.
neurips-2025-gre-suite-geo-localization-.tldr: GRE Suite combines geographic reasoning data, a staged vision-language model, and a benchmark to improve image geolocation across multiple scales.

paragraphs: Giving a language model many examples can improve its performance, but the sequence of those examples still matters. The paper experimentally confirms that demonstration-order instability persists in many-shot in-context learning, generally involving more than 50 examples. Larger context windows therefore do not by themselves eliminate sensitivity to example ordering.

The authors identify two obstacles to finding a good sequence. Existing heuristics based on model predictions become unreliable when long contexts make information difficult to use, and exhaustively checking possible orders is computationally infeasible. They introduce an information-theoretic evaluation metric designed to quantify how much usable information a particular ordering provides.

HIDO combines that metric with a hierarchical search over demonstration orders. This enables more refined exploration without evaluating every possible arrangement. Experiments involving multiple language models and real-world datasets report consistent, efficient improvements over other baselines. The work treats ordering as an optimization problem with both an explicit quality measure and a search strategy suited to large demonstration sets.
neurips-2025-hierarchical-demonstration-.tldr: HIDO uses an information-theoretic ordering metric and hierarchical search to improve many-shot prompting without checking every example permutation.

paragraphs: Shortcut models can generate samples in one, a few, or many steps using the same trained network. This flexibility is appealing, but the paper identifies several interacting training problems: guidance can compound and create artifacts, fixed guidance limits control, losses favor low-frequency content, self-consistency conflicts with exponential moving average training, and curved flow paths hinder convergence.

The proposed iSM framework assigns specific mechanisms to these problems. Intrinsic Guidance enables dynamic control over guidance strength and addresses its compounding. A multilevel wavelet loss targets the frequency bias to recover fine detail. Scaling Optimal Transport reduces training variance while encouraging straighter, more stable generation paths. Twin EMA addresses the tension between training stability and self-consistency.

Experiments on ImageNet at 256-by-256 resolution report substantial FID improvements over baseline shortcut models across all three sampling regimes. The findings support the combined framework’s effectiveness while retaining a single network’s sampling flexibility. The contribution is a coordinated training redesign addressing several identified bottlenecks together.
neurips-2025-improved-training-technique.tldr: iSM redesigns shortcut-model training to improve guidance, detail, and stability, with better reported image-generation results across sampling step counts.

paragraphs: Fair representation learning seeks to retain useful predictive information while reducing discrimination associated with a sensitive attribute. This paper introduces a kernel-based equalized-odds criterion, EO_k, to analyze how accuracy interacts with three fairness objectives. Independence concerns predictions and sensitive attributes; separation conditions that relationship on the true outcome; calibration conditions the outcome–attribute relationship on the prediction.

The analysis distinguishes whether the target outcome and sensitive attribute are statistically independent. Under independence, the authors show that EO_k satisfies both independence and separation. When those variables are dependent, they report preservation of predictive accuracy alongside lower bounds involving independence and calibration. The distinction makes the underlying statistical setting central to the trade-off characterization.

The paper also defines an empirical statistic computable in quadratic time, with linear-time approximations available. A concentration inequality supplies error bounds and guarantees for this estimate, supporting statistical fairness certificates. The contribution is primarily theoretical: it provides a measurable criterion and analytical groundwork for later algorithm design and empirical study.
neurips-2025-kernel-based-equalized-odds.tldr: A kernel-based equalized-odds criterion characterizes accuracy–fairness trade-offs and provides an empirical statistic with theoretical error guarantees.

paragraphs: Masked diffusion models produce outputs through iterative refinement, which can make generation slow when sampling follows a static schedule. KLASS changes the sampling procedure to recognize predictions that are already stable and confident. Its aim is to spend fewer iterations completing an output while retaining sample quality.

The method uses token-level KL divergence to identify those stable predictions and unmasks multiple tokens within an iteration. Because this adjustment happens during sampling, it requires no additional model training. The central idea is to let evidence about prediction stability determine which tokens can be resolved together, accelerating the existing model’s generation process.

On reasoning benchmarks, the authors report wall-clock speedups of up to 2.78 times while improving performance relative to standard greedy decoding. They also report state-of-the-art results among diffusion-based samplers. Additional evaluations cover text, image, and molecular generation, supporting applicability across the tested domains and models. The speed figure is a reported maximum, while the broader contribution is a training-free adaptive sampler.
neurips-2025-klass-kl-guided-fast-infere.tldr: KLASS accelerates masked diffusion sampling by unmasking multiple stable tokens at once, with reported speedups of up to 2.78 times.

paragraphs: Benchmark scores can be difficult to translate into the scale of work an AI system can handle. This paper proposes the 50%-task-completion time horizon: the typical human duration of tasks that a model completes successfully half the time. It anchors capability to expert human effort, rather than the model’s own runtime.

The researchers timed people with relevant expertise on tasks from RE-Bench, HCAST, and 66 new shorter tasks. Within this evaluation, frontier models such as o3 reached a horizon of about 110 minutes. The authors report that frontier horizons approximately doubled every seven months from 2019, with possible acceleration after 2024. They suggest reliability, recovery from mistakes, reasoning, and tool use as primary contributors.

The extrapolation is explicitly conditional. If the findings generalize to real-world software work, continuing the trend predicts automation of many month-long human tasks within five years of the study. The paper discusses external-validity limits and implications for dangerous capabilities. Its measured horizon and its longer-term forecast therefore carry different evidential strength.
neurips-2025-measuring-ai-ability-to-com.tldr: The paper measures AI task capability in expert-human completion time and finds rising horizons, with longer-term automation forecasts conditional on generalization.

paragraphs: Entity alignment identifies records in different knowledge graphs that refer to the same entity. Symbolic methods offer precision but struggle with sparse or structurally different graphs, while neural approaches face challenges with interpretability and uncertainty. NeuSymEA combines neural prediction and logical rules in a shared probabilistic framework.

The framework represents the truth scores of candidate alignments jointly in a rule-regulated Markov random field. It trains through variational expectation-maximization. In the expectation step, a neural model represents truth-score distributions and infers missing matches. In the maximization step, observed and inferred matches update rule weights. A logic-driven symbolic inference engine supports reasoning with longer rules.

This arrangement lets inferred alignments inform the rules while the rules help organize alignment reasoning under uncertainty. The authors report a 7.6% hit@1 improvement over strong baselines on DBP15K_ZH-EN. They also report 73.7% hit@1 on DBP15K_FR-EN with only 1% of pairs supplied as seed alignments, supporting the framework’s reported robustness when labeled starting matches are scarce.
neurips-2025-neusymea-neuro-symbolic-ent.tldr: NeuSymEA combines neural alignment predictions with probabilistic logical rules, improving reported entity matching even with few seed alignments.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning depends on experience that helps an agent understand its environment. Passive exploration methods try to improve learning by prioritizing underexplored material in a replay buffer, but the paper identifies limited sample diversity as a weakness. Modelic Generative Exploration, or MoGE, addresses that weakness by generating additional experience around important underexplored states.

MoGE has two components. A diffusion generator produces critical states using guidance from entropy and temporal-difference error. A one-step imagination world model then constructs transitions associated with those states, aiming for experiences consistent with the environment’s dynamics. This connects the choice of states worth learning about with the construction of transitions that an agent can learn from.

The method integrates with mainstream off-policy reinforcement learning algorithms without structural modifications. Experiments on OpenAI Gym and DeepMind Control Suite report significant gains in efficiency and performance on complex tasks. The stated contribution is an exploration augmentation that expands learning material, complementing the existing algorithm through generated states and model-constructed experiences.
neurips-2025-off-policy-reinforcement-le.tldr: MoGE generates important underexplored states and model-based transitions to improve the efficiency and performance of off-policy reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Diffusion-based sequential recommenders generate suggested next items from a user’s interaction history through repeated denoising. The paper attributes an efficiency–effectiveness trade-off to errors introduced by discretizing that process. TA-Rec addresses the issue with two training stages intended to enable one-step generation while maintaining useful recommendations.

During pretraining, Temporal Consistency Regularization encourages neighboring denoising steps to produce consistent results. This smooths the denoising function, allowing noise to be mapped to target items in one step with bounded error. During fine-tuning, Adaptive Preference Alignment adjusts the process toward user preferences, with adaptation based on preference-pair similarity and timesteps.

The stages address related but distinct problems: making a shortened generation process consistent and keeping its trajectory aligned with what users prefer. Extensive experiments report improvements in both computational efficiency and recommendation effectiveness. The findings support the combined objective as a way to mitigate the discretization-induced trade-off, rather than requiring the recommendation process to retain all of its original denoising steps.
neurips-2025-on-efficiency-effectiveness.tldr: TA-Rec combines denoising consistency and adaptive preference alignment to achieve effective one-step diffusion-based recommendation.

paragraphs: Neural architecture search seeks strong networks within a candidate space, but training every candidate is expensive. Training-free metrics offer cheaper estimates, although each captures only some architectural properties. Combining them can help, yet a single combination for the whole search space may overlook how differently individual architectures respond to those metrics.

PO-NAS optimizes the metric combination separately for each architecture. It uses multiple training-free metrics as auxiliary scores and updates their combinations with limited training data gathered during the search, without relying on benchmarks. Surrogate models provide efficient performance predictions, and an evolutionary algorithm uses those predictions to search large spaces.

The approach therefore combines inexpensive architectural signals with a limited amount of direct training evidence. Its per-architecture weighting is intended to preserve differences that a global metric mixture could miss. The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating effectiveness. Despite its use of training-free metrics, the full procedure includes training-based feedback; that feedback is central to how its performance estimates are adapted.
neurips-2025-per-architecture-training-f.tldr: PO-NAS adapts metric combinations to individual architectures and combines limited training feedback with surrogate-guided evolutionary search.

paragraphs: Diffusion-model personalization can generate images of particular identities or objects, creating risks of unauthorized use. Existing defenses perturb images to interfere with personalization, but the paper reports that clean images or simple transformations can undermine them. Anti-Personalized Diffusion Models, or APDM, instead modifies the target diffusion model to hinder personalization of specified subjects.

The authors first analyze a naive application of existing losses and show that it cannot ensure convergence for robust anti-personalization. They introduce Direct Protective Optimization, a loss intended to disrupt subject personalization while preserving generative quality. This gives the protective objective a formulation designed specifically for modifying the model.

A second component, Learning to Protect, alternates between personalization and protection paths. By simulating future personalization trajectories, it adaptively strengthens protection at successive steps. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance in preventing unauthorized personalization compared with existing methods. The results support protection built into the evaluated target model, with the alternating strategy preparing that model against subsequent personalization attempts.
neurips-2025-perturb-a-model-not-an-imag.tldr: APDM modifies a diffusion model through protective optimization and simulated personalization trajectories to resist unauthorized subject personalization.

paragraphs: Precise Information Control asks whether a language model can turn supplied claims into long-form text without introducing unsupported information. Its full setting requires inclusion of exactly all input claims, while its partial setting requires selecting only relevant ones. This separates faithful content control from the broader challenge of obtaining trustworthy source information.

PIC-Bench adapts eight generation tasks, including summarization and biography writing, to this setup using self-contained, verifiable input statements. Evaluations of open and proprietary models find input-unfaithful hallucinations in more than 70% of generations from state-of-the-art models. The result shows that providing well-formed claims alone did not ensure faithful generation in the tested setting.

The authors develop a post-training framework using weakly supervised preference data to train an 8B PIC-LM. Full-setting F1 improves from 69.1% to 91.0%. In end-to-end pipelines, they report a 17.1% improvement in exact-match recall for retrieval-assisted ambiguous question answering and a 30.5% improvement in factual precision for birthplace fact-checking, supporting the practical value of stronger information control.
neurips-2025-precise-information-control.tldr: PIC-Bench exposes frequent unsupported additions in long-form generation, while targeted post-training substantially improves adherence to supplied claims.

paragraphs: Optimizing instructions for a black-box language model requires evaluating prompts without access to its internal parameters. Some methods use a white-box model to turn adjustable soft prompts into written instructions. Multiple soft prompts can produce the same instruction, leading to repeated black-box evaluations of effectively identical candidates.

PRESTO uses that many-to-one relationship as information about the search space. The set of soft prompts producing one instruction is its preimage. The framework shares an instruction’s evaluation score across its preimage, chooses initial candidates to improve search-space coverage using preimage information, and regularizes score predictions to remain consistent within each preimage.

These components make one evaluation informative about multiple soft prompts and incorporate their equivalence into optimization. Under the same query budget, PRESTO observes 14 times as much scored data, according to the paper. Experiments on 33 instruction-optimization tasks report superior performance. The gain concerns the effective use of evaluations, rather than requiring 14 times as many distinct instructions to be queried.
neurips-2025-presto-preimage-informed-in.tldr: PRESTO improves black-box instruction optimization by sharing evaluation information among soft prompts that generate the same instruction.

paragraphs: Camera-based perception systems can struggle to place objects accurately in three dimensions because images do not provide explicit depth. This ambiguity also affects collaborative perception, where multiple participants contribute visual information. RayFusion focuses on using information from collaborators to reduce uncertainty about where objects lie along camera viewing rays.

The method fuses ray occupancy information supplied by collaborators. This information helps reduce redundant predictions and false positives along a ray, addressing the depth ambiguity that can otherwise weaken three-dimensional object detection. Its design targets the geometric uncertainty underlying those predictions while operating within a purely camera-based collaborative perception system.

Comprehensive experiments report consistent improvements over existing state-of-the-art models. Those findings support ray-based fusion as an effective way to improve detection in the evaluated collaborative setting. The paper’s contribution is a particular use of shared visual evidence: collaborators provide occupancy information that helps resolve ambiguous predictions along viewing directions, linking collaboration directly to the depth-estimation problem.
neurips-2025-rayfusion-ray-fusion-enhanc.tldr: RayFusion uses collaborators’ ray occupancy information to reduce depth ambiguity, redundant detections, and false positives in camera-based perception.

paragraphs: Low-Rank Adaptation reduces fine-tuning costs by restricting updates to a low-dimensional part of a pretrained weight matrix. The paper identifies a problem within that representation: low-rank factorizations are not unique, and their resulting weight updates can be inconsistent or imbalanced. The authors connect this behavior to slower convergence and reduced performance.

RefLoRA chooses a low-rank factorization at each step that minimizes an upper bound on the loss. This is a specific optimization criterion for the factorization, rather than a claim that each step globally minimizes the original training loss. The resulting updates are more consistent and balanced, and the method promotes a flatter loss landscape to support faster, stable convergence.

Experiments cover natural language understanding and commonsense reasoning using DeBERTaV3, LLaMA-7B, LLaMA2-7B, and LLaMA3-8B. The authors report faster convergence and stronger benchmark performance, with negligible additional computation relative to state-of-the-art LoRA variants. The findings suggest that improving the internal factorization can strengthen adaptation while retaining its computational advantages.
neurips-2025-reflora-refactored-low-rank.tldr: RefLoRA optimizes the low-rank factorization at each update to improve fine-tuning stability, convergence, and performance with negligible added computation.

paragraphs: Serving interactive language models at scale places substantial demand on server GPUs. SpecEdge brings consumer-grade edge GPUs into the serving process by dividing generation work between edge devices and servers. It uses speculative decoding, with edge devices drafting tokens and servers verifying them, while exchanging only token outputs over the network.

The framework coordinates these activities through two mechanisms. Proactive edge drafting overlaps token creation with server verification, allowing the two sides to work concurrently. Pipeline-aware scheduling interleaves multiple users’ requests to increase server throughput. Together, these mechanisms address both the timing of an individual request and the sharing of server resources across requests.

Against a server-only baseline, experiments report 2.22 times the server throughput and 1.91 times the overall cost efficiency. Inter-token latency also falls by 11.24%. These results connect the workload split to both serving capacity and interactive responsiveness in the evaluated system. The contribution is a coordinated serving framework that makes edge computation useful within a shared server pipeline.
neurips-2025-specedge-scalable-edge-assi.tldr: SpecEdge overlaps edge token drafting with server verification to improve serving throughput, cost efficiency, and inter-token latency.

paragraphs: Understanding real-world events requires reasoning about time amid dense information, rapidly changing circumstances, and dependencies between social interactions. TimE is a benchmark designed around these challenges. Its contribution is an evaluation structure that examines temporal reasoning across different scenarios and task types, making the capability more specific than a single overall score.

The benchmark contains 38,522 question–answer pairs organized into three levels and 11 detailed subtasks. Its three component datasets, TimE-Wiki, TimE-News, and TimE-Dial, reflect different real-world temporal challenges. This organization supports examining how model performance varies with the setting and the type of temporal reasoning required.

The authors evaluate both reasoning and non-reasoning models and analyze performance across scenarios and tasks. They also examine the effect of test-time scaling on temporal reasoning capabilities. A released human-annotated subset, TimE-Lite, supports further research and standardized evaluation. The stated outcome is a benchmark and accompanying analysis; the abstract does not establish a specific model ranking or direction of benefit from additional test-time computation.
neurips-2025-time-a-multi-level-benchmar.tldr: TimE evaluates language-model temporal reasoning through 38,522 question–answer pairs spanning multiple real-world scenarios, levels, and subtasks.
